title: LIN-4251 tidy-after: one endpoint-hint ladder and one closing lead-in in the preamble (the edges its blind read named)
description:
## Goal

The dispatch preamble's endpoint hints are written once, with "may the stage update the workspace?" as one optional clause rather than a second copy of the whole ladder; and the closing lines share their common lead-in.

## Context

Blind reads of LIN-4251 (`2f0c9d5b0`) scored it better and mixed. The "mixed" pass named three edge copies in `lib/proxy-preamble.js` and its tests:

* `readOnlyContextLines` is a second hand-written copy of `workContextLines`' six-branch endpoint-hint ladder, differing by one clause. It was made so that every `work` stage stayed byte-identical, a constraint set in the scope, not by the builder. The test that pinned "only the mandate and closing differ" was deleted, so a later hint change on the work side would quietly miss every non-work stage.
* `WRITES_BLOCK`'s four closings repeat the same two-line "runner reports back…" lead-in word for word, and the tests repeat all four as literals.
* `tests/unit/lin-4248-survey-stages.test.js` went back to a literal `['survey-task','survey-place']`.

This is the loop's "after" step: the copies a blind read names at a change's edges become a small tidy-after in the same area.

## This step

* **One hint ladder,** built once, with the update-the-workspace clause added only for `work`.
* `work`**'s dispatched text stays byte-identical:** the fixture `tests/fixtures/lin-4251-work-blocks.json` is the proof. The non-work stages' text may change trivially if one ladder needs it; say exactly how.
* **One closing lead-in,** shared by the four closings.
* **Tests read the Survey kinds from the templates'** `writes`**/**`route`**,** not a literal, unless a reason is recorded for the literal.
* Bring back a test that pins "only the mandate, closing and update clause differ from the work block".

**Not this ticket:** changing what any stage is told beyond that.

## Done when

* `readOnlyContextLines` is gone, or is a thin call into the one ladder.
* The work-block fixture is unchanged.
* The "only these differ" test is back.
* The closing lead-in exists once.

## How to go about it (from a Survey before work began)

Both Surveys (on this ticket, 14:24–14:25, at `473cc865e`) agree. The update clause isn't one suffix: it comes in three grammatical forms woven into hand-placed line breaks, and work is byte-frozen across 36 fixture keys. The person's scope call, in order:

1. **Capture first, at the base, before touching the ladder:**
   * a **non-work fixture** (the three non-work `writes` values across the same conditions), so "say exactly how the non-work text changed" is a diff;
   * the **"only the mandate, closing and update clause differ from work" test**, written against the current code over those conditions. It compares whitespace-normalised text with the clause's forms stated explicitly, not taken from the ladder (which would make it check itself). It should fail today only where the copy drifted.
2. **One positional ladder:** each branch as data with a clause slot, `work` filling it and the others leaving it empty. **No regex-stripping of rendered work text.** The work fixture is unchanged. The non-work line breaks may move (e.g. `/relations/…` onto its own line). That's the allowed trivial change: show the fixture diff, and add a row to `scripts/prompt-template-change-log.md` (and fix its LIN-4251 row, which still says "PR pending").
3. **One closing lead-in in the code** (the shared one-and-a-half lines). **The tests keep their literal copies** ("so a drift … fails here"): one literal lead-in plus a tail per value. Don't import the constant into the test.
4. **The Survey kinds stay a literal in** `lin-4248-survey-stages.test.js`**, with its reason extended** (the person's call, following both voices). Deriving them from `route === null` would make its "neither Survey has a route" assert prove itself, and would let a future hand-only one-comment stage join silently. This replaces the ticket's third bullet.
5. Update the comment that names `readOnlyContextLines` (about line 430) and the stale line references in `docs/prompt-pipeline/stage-descriptions/plumbing.md`.

**Not in this ticket** (both voices): building the hints as sentences wrapped once, which would collapse the eight branches but change work's text. It needs its own recorded change and a new fixture; to the tally.

## At merge (who else must learn about it)

* The work fixture is unchanged, the non-work fixture's diff is in the PR, and the change-log row is there.
* `readOnlyContextLines` is gone.
* The "only these differ" test is green.
* The closing lead-in exists once in the code.

## Implementation Plan

*Pruned at close-out; the full plan is preserved in the task snapshots (captured 2026-11-05T14:52:04Z) and the comment trail.*

Implemented as approved in [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2301](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2301>) (squash-merged as `0c3d3448`): one endpoint-hint ladder (`endpointHintParts` + `renderEndpointHints`), `readOnlyContextLines` removed, `CLOSING_LEAD_IN` shared by the four closings, the "only mandate, closing and clause differ" test restored, `SURVEYS` kept as a literal with its reason extended. Work fixture unchanged. Deviation: none in design; the restored test passes at base by design (whitespace-normalised), so the non-work line-break change is evidenced by the base-vs-head render diff in the PR and review instead.

### Session fit, review

fits one session

comments.body:
## Survey open-0: LIN-4277 @ 473cc865e

**Why it's harder than deleting a copy:** the update clause isn't a suffix you can tack on. In `workContextLines` (`lib/proxy-preamble.js:382-428`) it's woven into hand-placed line breaks, and it has two grammatical forms:
- with an identifier: `…, and update the workspace as you work (…).`. Sometimes it's split across lines (`…by text, and update the workspace` / `as you work (…).`, :397-398), and sometimes it's a line of its own (:390, :404).
- without an identifier: `… and to update the workspace…`, hanging off "Use the proxy to pull context". The break falls before, inside or after it depending on the branch (:411, :416, :422, :426-427).

With no width rule to recompute and `work` byte-frozen across 36 fixture keys, the one ladder has to hold work's line breaks as data. In practice, each branch becomes a list of lines with a clause slot, and the non-work text is whatever renders with the slot empty. That moves non-work line breaks. For example, `/relations/LIN-42.` drops onto its own line instead of joining `…raw detail` the way `readOnlyContextLines` does now (:268). That's the "trivial change" the ticket allows. Paste the non-work before/after, and add a row to `scripts/prompt-template-change-log.md`.

The shortcut to avoid is rendering work and regex-stripping `CLAUSE`. It trades a copy for string surgery that stays right only while the wording does.

**The "only these differ" test** has to state its diff exactly: mandate, closing, and the clause in both forms, with line breaks either normalised or pinned. Anything less is too loose, or another copy of the ladder.

**Closing lead-in:** folding the four rows (:203-234) is easy. But the test's `CLOSING` literals are deliberate: "Literal copies, so a drift in the constant text fails here" (test :28-29). I'd keep the lead-in once as a test literal and record why, because importing the constant would let the test pass whatever the text says.

**Survey kinds from `writes`/`route`:** at base, `writes==='one-comment' && route===null` gives exactly `survey-task` and `survey-place`: `context` is one-comment but routed, and `retro` is unrouted but `none`. But `lin-4248-survey-stages.test.js:48-49` asserts `route === null`. Selecting the kinds by `route===null` makes that assert prove nothing, and a future hand-only one-comment stage would join silently. The ticket allows the literal with a recorded reason, and that is the honest result here. If deriving, use `writes` plus an explicit exclusion, not `route`.

**Symptom vs cause:** the copy exists because the hints are hand-wrapped prose under a byte-freeze, so presentation (line breaks) is welded to wording. Every future hint tidy will fight the fixture the same way. That's not this ticket.

**First move:** before touching the ladder, write the new "only mandate, closing and clause differ" test against the current code, over the 36 fixture conditions × the 3 non-work values. It should fail today only on line breaks, and that failure is exactly the non-work diff the one ladder will produce. Then fold the ladder until the fixture and that test both pass.

## Survey global: LIN-4277 @ 473cc865e

**Where it lands.** In `lib/proxy-preamble.js`, between `WRITES_BLOCK` and the end of `buildProxyContextPreamble` (:200–481). Also in the two `lin-4248-survey-*` tests and in `lin-4251-writes-entrances.test.js`, which holds the work fixture. Over one day, 4248 → 4253 → 4251 improved the area: traits are declared once and the preamble has no stage names. But 4251 left it half-tidied. The work ladder is eight hand-wrapped branches, and `readOnlyContextLines` is a re-wrapped second copy of it.

**What the obvious way runs into.**
- **The clause isn't one string.** In the work variants it shows up as `, and update…`, ` and update…` or ` and to update…`, and some variants break the line inside it. Keeping work byte-identical means each position has to choose `work ? a : b`. The non-work hints will then most likely take on work's line breaks (`…full raw detail\nand /relations/LIN-42.`). Nothing would notice, because non-work hint text is checked only by regexes. **Capture a non-work fixture at BASE first.** Then "say exactly how it changed" is a diff.
- **The restored "only these differ" test** can't reuse 2f0c9d5b's simple `.replace()`, because the clause text differs per variant. It has to compare whitespace-normalised text. Taking the clause from the ladder instead makes the test partly check itself.
- **The closing lead-in is 1½ lines.** Line 2 shares only the prefix `need to curl anything to phone home. Just END with `.
- **The test `CLOSING` literals are deliberate** ("so a drift … fails here"). Keep one literal lead-in in the test plus a tail per value, rather than importing the lead-in.
- **`SURVEYS` already has a recorded reason** (stages test :23–25). Deriving it from `one-comment && route===null` makes :48–49 ("neither Survey has a route") prove itself. It would also quietly let a future hand-only one-comment stage into the set. Either assert the derived set on its own, or keep the literal and extend the reason.

**Who else has to learn about it.** The comment at :430 names `readOnlyContextLines`; nothing imports it. `scripts/prompt-template-change-log.md` needs a row if any non-work rendered text changes, even if only line breaks change. Its LIN-4251 row still says "PR pending" although it landed as 2f0c9d5b. The line references in `plumbing.md` :135 are already stale, and this change will shift them again.

**Better, within reach:** a positional one-ladder, a non-work fixture, a shared lead-in prefix and a change-log row.

**Better still, not this ticket's:** the copies come from pinning hard-wrapped prose byte for byte. Hints built as sentences and wrapped once would collapse the eight branches. That changes work's text, so it needs its own recorded change and a new fixture.

LIN-4277 implemented — PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2301 (branch feat/lin-4277-endpoint-hint-ladder, commit fe62ba8b).

- One endpoint-hint ladder replaces readOnlyContextLines and the work ladder; work bytes unchanged (lin-4251-work-blocks.json, 36 keys green).
- Non-work hints: line breaks only, measured over 108 blocks (60 identical, 48 line-break-only, 0 word changes). Closings byte-identical.
- One shared closing lead-in (CLOSING_LEAD_IN); restored "only mandate, closing and clause differ" test; mutation witnesses run.
- CI on the PR: all 7 checks pass (CI success, Unit tests, E2E shards 1-4, Secret scan). Local: test:unit 23,705 pass; test:hermetic:keyed 23,705 pass.
- Note: the restored test passes at base by design (whitespace-normalised); the line-break change is covered by the before/after diff in the PR body, not the test.

## Review — LIN-4277

Reviewed PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2301 at head `fe62ba8bbad98712951cb0cbfd22282b05626cc8` (base `473cc865`, which is current `main`). The PR is **open, not merged**. The brief says it has landed; it has not.

CI: green on `fe62ba8b`. All 7 checks pass: Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan, and CI success.

### Scope vs plan
The changed files match the plan's places. `lib/proxy-preamble.js` has one ladder (`endpointHintParts` + `renderEndpointHints`, with clause pairs as data and no regex-stripping), `readOnlyContextLines` is gone, and `CLOSING_LEAD_IN` is the lead-in, written once. In the tests, the survey-preamble test has the restored "only these differ" test, plus a literal lead-in and one tail per value. Its only import is `WRITES`, alongside the existing imports; it does not import the constant. The survey-stages test keeps `SURVEYS` as a literal and extends its reason with the `route` half. The fixture `tests/fixtures/lin-4251-work-blocks.json` is untouched. Two other test files changed, and those edits are comment-only (renames of `contextLines` → endpoint hints). That is not overrun. Nothing else in `lib routes public scripts` carries the hint or closing text, so this change is isolated (no sibling copies).

### Independent checks (my runs, not the author's numbers)
- **Base vs head render:** I rendered `buildProxyContextPreamble` from `origin/main` and from the PR over 4 writes values × issue/none × prose/mcp × 8 flag combinations × providerUi set/null (256 blocks).
  - `work`: 64/64 byte-identical.
  - Non-work: 0 word changes. The only differences are line breaks.
  - Closings: byte-identical in all 256.
  - No blank lines were introduced.
  - This confirms the PR's "line breaks only" claim (60 unchanged / 48 line-break-only over its 108 blocks).
- **Targeted suites** (survey-preamble, writes-entrances, survey-stages, proxy-preamble, feedback-route): 357/357 pass.
- **Mutations** (run on survey-preamble and writes-entrances, each reverted; tree clean afterwards):
  - Non-work `otherwise` '.' → '': 96 fail.
  - Non-work renders the work clause: 134 fail.
  - One word changed in the code's `CLOSING_LEAD_IN`: 140 fail. This proves the test does not import the constant.
  - Non-work drift (`otherwise` → ' via the proxy.'): 96 fail.
  - One word changed in a work clause: 23 fail (the fixture).
- **Regression check:** `git log` on the touched files shows only 4248, 4253 and 4251 before this change, and nothing since the ticket was created. LIN-2804 capability gating and the `!== false` defaults are kept.
- **Note:** the restored test passes at base, as the author says. The plan expected it to fail on line breaks, but a whitespace-normalised comparison cannot see line breaks, so that expectation contradicted the plan's own design. The line-break claim is proven by the render diff above instead. Not a defect.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside** (plan step 5, stale line refs in plumbing.md). `docs/prompt-pipeline/stage-descriptions/plumbing.md:135` was updated, but the new numbers are off by one or two from the declarations at the head. They read `attachProxyContext` `:724`, `provisionResumeCredential` `:817`, `buildProxyContextPreamble` `:364`. They should be **`:723`, `:816`, `:366`** (check with `grep -n "^export.*function \(attachProxyContext\|provisionResumeCredential\|buildProxyContextPreamble\)" lib/proxy-preamble.js`). Settle before the merge: close-out makes the edit. No CI check covers doc line refs.
- **Inside** (plan step 5, change-log rows). The new LIN-4277 row in `scripts/prompt-template-change-log.md` says "PR pending (branch `feat/lin-4277-endpoint-hint-ladder`)". That is the same stale pattern this PR just fixed in the 4248, 4253 and 4251 rows. Settle at merge: close-out changes it to `` `<merge sha>` (#2301) ``.
- **Inside** (Done-when "non-work changes trivially; say exactly how"). The line-break-only claim is not asserted by any test, because the restored test is whitespace-normalised. **Discharged** by my independent base-vs-head render above: 0 word changes, closings and work byte-identical.

Nothing needs a post-deploy check. This is a pure string builder, fully exercised by the unit suites. Rollback: revert `fe62ba8b` (or its squash commit); no data or migration is involved.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger. The work meets every Done-when item and the load-bearing tests fail under mutation. Two small inside fixes remain (the plumbing.md line refs `:723`/`:816`/`:366`, and the LIN-4277 change-log row set to its merge sha and #2301).

## Close-out — LIN-4277

**Merged:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2301, squash commit `0c3d3448b3f3cdfe2a97a09a4975113c73e723c9`, pinned with `--match-head-commit 6562fadd`.

**Changes I made after the Approve** (commit `6562fadd`, both answer the review's two inside items):
- `docs/prompt-pipeline/stage-descriptions/plumbing.md:135`: refs corrected to `attachProxyContext` `:723`, `provisionResumeCredential` `:816`, `buildProxyContextPreamble` `:366` (re-checked with grep against the head).
- `scripts/prompt-template-change-log.md`: LIN-4277 row now reads `PR #2301` instead of "PR pending (branch …)". Deviation from the review's wording: a squash sha cannot be written before the merge without a second commit to main, so I used the PR number, the form the LIN-4021 row uses; the sha is `0c3d3448` (recorded here).

**Ledger:**
- plumbing.md line refs (inside): fixed as above.
- Change-log row (inside): fixed as above (PR number, not sha).
- Non-work change is line breaks only (inside): discharged by the review's independent base-vs-head render (256 blocks: work 64/64 byte-identical, 0 word changes, closings identical); not re-run by me.
- Post-deploy: review names none (pure string builder). Rollback: revert `0c3d3448`.

**CI:** green on the exact head `6562fadd` before merge: Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan, CI success (7/7). Not re-run on the merge commit on main.

**Housekeeping:** description snapshot verified in task snapshots (15,613-char pre-prune capture) before pruning; Implementation Plan body replaced by a stub (heading, `fits one session` and `plan-review due: no` kept). No related tickets to close; no outside follow-ups (the review's ledger had none; the hint-as-sentences idea was already marked out of scope).

## Survey 1a (round 3)

**1. Why was it difficult?** It mostly wasn't. The constraint was work's byte-freeze: 36 fixture keys, with the update clause woven into hand-placed line breaks in three grammatical forms. A suffix or regex couldn't express that, so each branch became text plus a clause slot, with the newlines inside the strings. Once the slot sat where work already broke the line, the fixture went green on the first run. The real friction was elsewhere. The witness the plan predicted (the restored test failing at base on line breaks) can't exist, because the test compares whitespace-normalised text. So I captured the 108 non-work blocks to scratch before and after, and diffed them.

**2. What first?** Capture the non-work baseline before touching `lib/`, which I did. I'd also ask, before writing it, whether the restored test could fail at base at all. That would have moved the line-break proof onto the diff from the start, not after the test came back green.

**3. What I'd tidy.** `updateClause` always has `otherwise: '.'`, so the pair is really a work-only tail; it could be a single string. The same file now enumerates the 16 endpoint variants twice (the CLAUSE-gating block and my `ENDPOINT_VARIANTS`), and the fixture test has a third copy. `plumbing.md` cites line numbers that will rot again; it should cite symbol names.

**4. The ticket if the area were right.** The hints would be sentences, joined or wrapped by code, and the fixture would pin normalised text rather than layout. "Drop the update clause for non-work" would then be one conditional with no ladder at all. Any second copy would be a two-line delete.

**5. What the ticket/plan got wrong.** The predicted failing-at-base witness contradicted its own "compare normalised" rule. The data model it sketched ("a line is a list of parts; drop empty lines") was more than needed: newlines inside parts plus a full-stop slot covered every branch. Its line citations were already stale, though it said so. The rest held.

**6. What it left behind.** Things that got simpler: the non-work hints now derive from work's, `readOnlyContextLines` is gone, and the net change is slightly negative. In two places on purpose: the closing lead-in lives in code and as a literal in the test. In three places by accident: the endpoint-variant enumeration. Stale: my own change-log row says "PR pending" though it landed as `0c3d3448`, the same staleness I corrected on three neighbours; many older rows still say it too. `docs/papers` still quotes `readOnlyContextLines` as historical text. The `finalizePrompt :1032-1043` citation points at a callback that starts at :1025; I left it.

**7. Was the tidy-after worth it?** The code change was cheap: one file, an hour of real work. It was dwarfed by the two Surveys, the plan and the witnesses around it. Inside LIN-4251 it would have been cheaper still. The copy came from the byte-identical rule plus the deleted "only these differ" test, and building the slot there would have cost about what writing the copy did. To make it smaller: keep the guarding test when you split a path, and pin wording rather than wrapping, so a second layout never looks safer than sharing one.
